fields.meta_description: Build a demo landing page that shows the product before the form. See a video demo, a product tour, a group demo, and pages by industry.
fields.h1: Build a Demo Landing Page That Shows Before It Asks
fields.hero_description: Build a demo landing page that puts the product on screen first and saves every demo request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts on a Demo Page
fields.features_subheading: A demo landing page shows the product, then asks for a call or a seat. Emergent builds the page and the request table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
A page built from how you sell

Describe the product and the demo you run, whether it is recorded or live. Emergent builds the page in that order, and the product stays on screen above the request form.
fields.feature_2:
Request buttons that carry their place

Give each button on the page a name, such as chapter-3 or pricing. Every request saves the name of its button. Sort by it to see which part of the demo made people ask.
fields.feature_3:
Every demo request saved as a row

Each request lands as a row in a database you own, with the buyer's work email and the time it arrived. Filter the rows by week, then sort them by company before Monday.
fields.feature_4:
An email to the rep who owns the account

Name a rep for each territory or company size, and the app emails that rep when a request arrives. Slack and in-app alerts work the same way, with a reminder after a day.
fields.feature_5:
Seat limits for live sessions

Set a seat count for each live session. The page shows how many seats are left, closes the session once it is full, and moves new signups to the next date on your list.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the page and its request table to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Or keep it hosted on Emergent on your own domain, which uses credits, and keep editing it by prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Demo Landing Page Examples by Format
fields.tab_content_1:
After chapter 3 came 14 of 31 requests

Lanthorn Brewlog shows a 7-minute demo video in 4 chapters, with no form in front of it. Each chapter has its own Book a live demo button, and every request saves the chapter it came from. Chapter 3 drew 14 of this week's 31 requests, one of them from Pirjo Haverlake, who runs 3 taprooms.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four tour screens come before any form

Pennygrove's page asks for nothing until the tour ends. The clinic scheduling tool clicks through 4 screens: the calendar, reminder texts, the waitlist, and reports. Screen 5 asks for a work email and the number of providers. Danuta Wystan sent one for 6 providers, and the app emailed it to Tilde Marren.
fields.tab_content_3:
Seat 41 goes into next Wednesday's demo

Every Wednesday at 11:00 am, Quarryline demos its invoicing software for landscapers to a live group of 40. The page counts down the seats left. This week filled by Monday, and seat 41 and every signup after it went to next Wednesday. That session has 9 so far, and Maelle Eskildsen took seat 9.
fields.tab_content_4:
Requests from all three trades land in one table

Corbelle sells one booking tool to three trades, with a demo page for each: dental offices, salons, and physical therapy clinics. The dental page leads with "Fill every open chair this week." Every request lands in one table with a column for its page. October brought 49: 23 dental, 17 salon, and 9 physical therapy.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Demo Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a demo landing page that shows the product before it asks for a call, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what to show before the ask
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Record the demo in short chapters
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only what the call needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a visitor should see before you ask for anything: a recorded video, a click-through tour, or a seat in a live session. Pick one as the main path at the top of the page. The other two can sit lower down as second options.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Split the recording into short chapters, each about one job the buyer does. Name each chapter after that job, such as taproom counts, rather than a menu in your product. Put a request button under every chapter, so a viewer can ask at the point that caught them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Keep the request form to what your rep reads before the call: who the person is, how to reach them at work, the size of the team, and one question about the current setup. Leave the rest for the call, where a person can ask follow-ups.
fields.howto_step_4_des: If you sell to more than one industry, write a version of the page for each, with its own headline and screenshots from that trade. Keep the form identical on every version, so all requests land in one table and compare cleanly by page.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent what the page should hold: the video or tour, the form fields, who gets each request, and any seat limit for live sessions. Emergent returns the finished page, with a table for the requests, in one pass. Change any part later by prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set a reply target for the team
fields.howto_step_6_des: Agree how fast a rep answers a request, such as within one business day, and say so under the form. The app can send that rep a reminder when a request sits past the target. The request table shows which ones are still waiting.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go through the page as a buyer
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the page goes live, open it on a phone and act like a buyer: play the chapters, then submit the form from one of the buttons. Check that the row lands in the table with the right chapter, and that the rep's email arrives.

faq_plan.q: What is a demo landing page?
faq_plan.a: A demo landing page is a single web page that shows a product to potential buyers and asks for one next step, such as booking a live demo or joining a group session. It puts the product on screen, in a video or a tour, right beside the request form.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a demo landing page?
faq_plan.a: Choose first how buyers will see the product: on video, in a tour of screens, or in a live session. Then describe the product and who answers each request to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It sets up the page and the form, and stores every request as a row you can sort.

faq_plan.q: What should a demo landing page include?
faq_plan.a: A headline that names who the product is for, the product itself on screen, and one request button repeated down the page. Add a short list of what the demo covers and how long it takes. Emergent builds those sections from a description, and each request is kept in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How is a demo landing page different from a product homepage?
faq_plan.a: It has one job where a homepage has many. Keep the demo page on getting a buyer to see the product and ask for a call, and leave the company story and wider links to the homepage. Use a saas landing page to sell the product as a whole, with a trial if you offer one.

faq_plan.q: Should a demo landing page ask for an email before the video plays?
faq_plan.a: Not at first: start with the video open. An open video lets a buyer judge the product first and ask from the moment that caught them. A gated video asks for the email up front, before the visitor has seen the product. Try each for a few weeks on the same page and compare the requests your reps would accept.

faq_plan.q: How long should the video on a demo landing page be?
faq_plan.a: Short enough to watch in one sitting. Split a longer demo into chapters of a few minutes each, one per job the buyer does, and list the chapters beside the video. A viewer can then jump straight to the part they came for and skip the rest.

faq_plan.q: Can a demo landing page let visitors try the product instead of watching it?
faq_plan.a: A page built that way can. A click-through tour of real screens, or a sandbox with sample data, lets a visitor use the product before asking for a call. For an API, a developer landing page with a request box that returns real output does the same job. Emergent builds the tour screens and the form from a prompt.

faq_plan.q: When should a demo landing page offer a group demo instead of one-on-one calls?
faq_plan.a: When more people ask than you can meet one by one, or when every first call is the same walk-through. A weekly group session with a seat limit covers the general tour. Keep one-on-one calls for buyers who need their own setup discussed.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which part of a demo landing page brings in requests?
faq_plan.a: Tag every request with the spot it came from, such as a video chapter or the pricing section. Then count the week's requests by tag. Emergent builds the form so each request keeps its tag, stored in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should each industry get its own demo landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when buyers in each industry do different work with the product. Give each version a headline and screenshots that match the industry, and keep the form the same. A crm landing page for real estate teams, for instance, could show listings and showings, where one for agencies could show client projects.

plan.angle: The top 10 for demo landing page are example roundups and anatomy guides for SaaS request-a-demo pages (Instapage, SeedProd, Spectra, Saleo, SaaSFrame): they list what a good page carries but hand over no working page. This page shows four demo landing pages built from a prompt, each one putting the product on screen before the ask: a video demo in chapters with a request button under each chapter, a five-screen click-through tour that ends on a request screen, a weekly group demo that closes at 40 seats, and one demo page per industry feeding one request table. The Form hub's demo request form owns the form itself (booking on submit, email checks, presenter prep, no-shows), so this page stays on the page around it: what to show, in what order, and for whom. Free trial and SaaS pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

Pennygrove, scheduling software for clinics, runs a click-through tour of 4 screens before any form; a fifth screen asks for a name, a work email and the number of providers, and Danuta Wystan's request for a clinic with 6 providers was saved and emailed to the account rep, Tilde Marren.
